title: Tesla FSD in Europe: Germany is on board, the EU waits
subtitle: What Germany agreed with Tesla, what the EU did not decide, and what happens next.
title_narration: Tesla F.S.D. in Europe. Germany is on board. The E.U. waits.
as_of: Grounded in Jim's Interest Journal research for Tue Oct 6, 2026. Regulatory status may change; the EU decision is expected in December.

scenes.label: Tuesday, Oct 6
scenes.heading: Germany backs *EU approval* of FSD

lines: The EU committee met, with *no vote*.
A decision is now expected in *December*.

scenes.caption: Germany now backs EU approval of Tesla's FSD. The EU committee met with no vote, and a decision is now expected in December.
evidence: FSD in Europe: Germany backs EU approval; the EU committee met with no vote, and a decision is now expected in December.

scenes.label: The German deal
scenes.heading: Agreed with Tesla in September

cards.label: the most FSD may exceed the speed limit
responsible: the driver, per the ministry

scenes.caption: Germany's transport ministry said it reached agreement with Tesla in September. FSD may exceed the speed limit by at most 10%, and the driver stays 100 percent responsible.
evidence: Germany's transport ministry said Tuesday it reached agreement with Tesla in September.
FSD may exceed the speed limit by at most 10%, and the driver stays "100 percent responsible."

scenes.label: A new name for Europe?

data.who: the name the ministry says Tesla offered; Tesla hasn't announced it

scenes.caption: The ministry also said Tesla offered to rename the system Tesla Assisted Driving in Europe. Tesla hasn't announced that.
evidence: The ministry also said Tesla offered to rename the system "Tesla Assisted Driving" in Europe; Tesla hasn't announced that.

evidence: Minister Bilger said earlier Tuesday he'd consider a German-only route if the EU fails.
The ministry's written statement commits only to the EU process and doesn't approve FSD in Germany.
